Greetings.

Thank you for bringing us this excellent article, and it definitely deserves a +1! I have translated it to SCP Foundation Chinese branch, see here for the translated version.

There is something I didn't quite get in your document. The Arabic in the last page,

الله الأب (THE IMMUTABLE, THE INFINITE, THE EVERLASTING)

It means God the Father, or Allāh al-ab, which is used by Arabic-speaking Christians. (You may refer to Wikipedia, article "Allah", section Christianity) I assume the Jibril is a Muslim, so it is not likely that he would use the term "God the Father".. Is it a mistake, or there are deep meanings?

Perhaps it would be better using only "الله" ? Or you may refer to Allah's other names if you want to change the word..

Hi-

Don't know if the author will see this, but "imam" in the Shi'ite sense is very different to "imam" in the Sunni sense. "Imam" refers to those members of Muhammad's line who Shi'ites believe are the rightful heads of the Islamic community- not to a religious dignitary. I know it's a small thing, but using it to mean a religious official or a cleric, as is done here, is rather immersion breaking. "Mullah" or even "Ayatollah" would perhaps be better.
